images.filename: 2000-06-10 01 Watermen returning from lobster fishing to Tangier Island, Virginia USA.jpg
images.caption: Watermen on the BARBARA ANNETTE, returning from fishing on the Chesapeake Bay on June 10, 2000, entering the harbor at Tangier Island, Virginia USA. In the background, Tangier Island Cruises brings visitors on the CHESAPEAKE BREEZE from Buzzard Point Marina in Reedsville, Virginia. Typical catches are blue crabs, fish, and oysters.
images.alt: Watermen on the BARBARA ANNETTE, returning from fishing on the Chesapeake Bay on June 10, 2000, entering the harbor at Tangier Island, Virginia USA. images.caption: TANGIER, Va. – Aerial imagery of the Uppards portion of Tangier Island shows a breach where waters from the Chesapeake Bay flow into interior portions of the land. Each time a dredging occurs the Norfolk District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, uses dredged material gathered from the navigation channel at the island to help plug the breach.  (U.S. Army photo/Patrick Bloodgood)

images.caption: TANGIER, Va. â Remnants of a well from the town of Canaan, which has been swallowed up by the rising waters of the Chesapeake Bay decades ago, sits along what is now the northern shoreline of the Uppards portion of Tangier Island here October 14, 2016. Scientists estimate the rest of the now inhabited island will become uninhabitable over the next 25 to 50 years if something is not done to help keep the island above water. (U.S. Army photo/Patrick Bloodgood)

images.caption: TANGIER, Va. - Tidal waters flood yards in this small Chesapeake Bay island fishing community here September 16, 2016. The community of roughly 470 residents are experiencing the impacts of sea level rise, erosion and land subsidence. Scientists estimate the island may become uninhabitable over the next 25 to 50 years if something is not done to help keep the island above water. (U.S. Army photo/Patrick Bloodgood)
